title: Angles from Intersecting Chords Assessment
description: Show mastery of finding interior chord angles and missing intercepted arcs in circles.

questions.question: Two chords intersect inside a circle. An angle intercepts arcs of 72 degrees and 108 degrees. What is the angle measure?
Which expression correctly finds an interior angle formed by intersecting chords with intercepted arcs 85 degrees and 45 degrees?
questions.explanation: Interior chord angles use half the sum of the two intercepted arcs.

questions.question: Two intercepted arcs measure 114 degrees and 36 degrees. Enter the interior angle measure in degrees.
An angle formed by two chords intersecting inside a circle is found by taking half the difference of the intercepted arcs.
questions.explanation: That is a common mix-up with exterior angle relationships. Inside the circle, use half the sum.

questions.question: An interior chord angle measures 74 degrees. One intercepted arc measures 52 degrees. What is the other intercepted arc?
questions.explanation: The intercepted arcs sum to 2(74) = 148 degrees. The missing arc is 148 - 52 = 96 degrees.

questions.question: An interior chord angle measures 82 degrees. One intercepted arc is 100 degrees. Enter the other intercepted arc in degrees.
questions.explanation: The arc sum is 2(82) = 164 degrees. The missing arc is 164 - 100 = 64 degrees.

questions.question: Chords AB and CD intersect at P. If angle APC uses arcs AC and BD, which arcs are used to find the vertical angle BPD?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles formed by the same intersecting chords use the same opposite arc pair, so angle BPD also uses arcs AC and BD.

questions.question: If two intercepted arcs for an interior chord angle have measures 40 degrees and 140 degrees, the angle is a right angle.
questions.explanation: 1/2(40 + 140) = 1/2(180) = 90 degrees, so the angle is right.

questions.question: Two chords intersect inside a circle. One angle is formed using intercepted arcs of 30 degrees and 150 degrees. What can you conclude about its vertical angle?
questions.explanation: The original angle is 1/2(30 + 150) = 90 degrees. Its vertical angle is congruent, so it is also 90 degrees.

questions.question: Two chords intersect inside a circle. An angle has measure 68 degrees, and its intercepted arcs are x degrees and 88 degrees. Enter x.
questions.explanation: Set 68 = 1/2(x + 88). Double to get 136 = x + 88, so x = 48.

questions.question: A student says an interior chord angle with intercepted arcs 112 degrees and 44 degrees measures 156 degrees. Explain the mistake and give the correct angle.
questions.correctAnswer: The student added the arcs but forgot to take half of the sum. The correct angle is 1/2(112 + 44) = 1/2(156) = 78 degrees.
questions.explanation: The key correction is that an interior chord angle is half the sum, not the full sum.

questions.question: Two chords intersect inside a circle. An angle measures 70 degrees. One intercepted arc measures 95 degrees. Find the other intercepted arc and show your equation.
questions.correctAnswer: Let the missing arc be x. Since 70 = 1/2(95 + x), double both sides to get 140 = 95 + x. Therefore x = 45 degrees.
questions.explanation: A complete solution should double the angle first, then subtract the known arc.
